examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}にレポートを{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: I handed the report to the teacher.

examples.japanese: {船|ふね}で{人|ひと}を{渡|わた}す。
{川|かわ}を{渡|わた}す{橋|はし}を{架|か}ける。
examples.english: To build a bridge that spans the river.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さな{船|ふね}で{旅人|たびびと}を{対岸|たいがん}に{渡|わた}す{仕事|しごと}をしている。
examples.english: He has the job of ferrying travelers to the other bank in a small boat.

notes:
{渡|わた}す means to hand over or pass something to someone.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pair: {渡|わた}る (intransitive, to cross)

MEANINGS:
1. To hand over: {書類|しょるい}を{渡|わた}す (hand over documents)
2. To ferry across: {人|ひと}を{対岸|たいがん}に{渡|わた}す (ferry someone across)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に～を{渡|わた}す: to hand X to someone
- {手|て}{渡|わた}す: to hand directly
- {引|ひ}き{渡|わた}す: to hand over (formal/legal)
- {受|う}け{渡|わた}す: to deliver, pass on

PARTICLE USAGE:
Aを Bに{渡|わた}す: to hand A to B
